  1. Description

Interface Kind<F,A>

All Known Implementing Classes:
CallableK, IO, ListK, OptionalK
public interface Kind<F,A>
F applied to A: how forj writes a higher-kinded type such as "some F<A>" where F is itself a type parameter. Java has no F<_>, so F is a witness: the raw class of the type constructor (List, IO, Optional), and Kind<List, A> stands for List<A>.

Types forj owns implement it directly (IO<A> implements Kind<IO, A>); JDK types are wrapped (ListK). Code rarely mentions it: the plugin's F<_> syntax writes F<A> for Kind<F, A>, and forj comprehensions wrap and unwrap for you.
